task.title: Attribute workflow-run starts to active tasks
task.objective: Complete issues https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/716 and https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/717 by recording immutable task provenance without coupling task and workflow-run lifecycles.
acceptance_criteria: Require an exact existing active task before creating an attributed workflow run.
Atomically reject a task revision race without creating the run stream.
Persist and replay exact task identity while preserving payload-version-1 unassociated starts.
Expose attribution through exact load, deterministic list, and typed history without adding execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused workflow-run target failed to compile because the attributed start API, task projection, typed precondition errors, and task started history variant did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for active, missing, terminal, malformed, legacy, reopen, listing, history, and deterministic task revision race behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Reusing the event log guarded append primitive allowed run creation to depend atomically on the observed active-task revision without a secondary association stream.
attempts.patch: Added start_for_task, payload version 2 task identity, fail-closed replay, task aware history, typed errors, ADR-0017, and milestone documentation.

attempts.summary: Preserved lifecycle and compatibility boundaries through review.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent and CodeRabbit review found no actionable implementation issue at the reviewed head.
attempts.patch: Kept legacy unassociated starts replayable and left task completion, workflow execution, lifecycle synchronization, retries, and scheduling outside the slice.

outcome.summary: Workflow-run starts can now carry immutable, atomically validated active-task provenance while both aggregate lifecycles remain independent.

lessons: Provenance is strongest when persisted at the authorization boundary rather than attached later.
A guarded cross-stream append prevents attribution to work that became terminal during run creation.
Payload versioning can add immutable provenance while retaining exact legacy replay.
Attribution does not imply lifecycle synchronization, execution ownership, scheduling, or permission.
